sara: Heads-up — noticed ~1-2% of streaming chat sessions drop mid-func-call handshake and client sees `event: end` without final tool payload. Anyone else seen this?

sara: Repro (very minimal): start a convo with a function/tool, streaming enabled, then send a few concurrent requests. Sometimes the final `func_payload` never arrives and stream ends. Example event sequence we *expect*:
```
EVENT: message.delta (text chunks)
EVENT: function_call.start (meta)
EVENT: function_call.payload (json)
EVENT: end
```
and what we sometimes get:
```
EVENT: message.delta
EVENT: function_call.start
EVENT: end
```

mike: Can you paste a request-id + any runtime log lines? Also which runtime version/region?

sara: req-id `req-7f9a2`, runtime `rdw-runtime-v2.14`, region `us-west-2`. I grabbed a truncated log: "[5801234510] req-7f9a2 stream: func_call_start -> kv-cache miss -> end (no payload)"

mike: ok, that helps. @ajay any idea if recent batching changes could drop the last chunk under backpressure?

ajay: I saw a similar signal last week during a burst test. Suspect continuous-batching + prefetch window race. There was an edge where the worker would consider the call complete when it had no more tokens buffered. If the payload writes to the stream after that decision, the event never flushes.

ajay: Quick checks: increase `stream_flush_timeout_ms` in the runtime to 200ms locally and repro. If it disappears, we likely need a stronger flush barrier on func_call completion.

katie: assigning myself to the API contract side — there's an open PR to make function_call terminal state explicit (add `final: true` event field). PR #432. Will coordinate with runtime.

oliver: Another mitigation: include incremental `seq_no` on stream events so clients can detect gaps and request the final payload via non-stream endpoint if gap seen. Small patch to add `x-stream-seq` header + `final` flag in body should be low-risk.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rdw-runtime-v2.14 -> prod (5801234000).

mike: @sara can you upload the full raw capture (server + client) to the incident bucket? Also include the client's library version.

sara: uploaded s3://redwood-debug/5801234567/req-7f9a2-trace.log.gz (client lib 1.8.2).

ajay: Thanks. I'll run a quick replay harness with `stream_flush_timeout_ms=200` and with/without batching to isolate. If I can reproduce locally I'll open a runtime PR for a flush barrier.

mike: If ajay can't repro, we should try oliver's seq_no fallback and katie's `final` flag in parallel. Low-risk server-side header + client patch to poll final endpoint on gap.

sara: ack. tagging @katie for contract change and @oliver for the minimal header patch.

katie: I'll update the contract doc to require `final: true|false` on terminal events and add a note that payloads may be delivered in a separate `function_call.payload` event. Will add compatibility guidance for older clients.

oliver: I'll prototype the `x-stream-seq` header on top of current streaming wire and add a tiny integration test that simulates a dropped chunk.

mike: can someone add a quick smoke test in the CI harness that verifies "end without payload" triggers fetching final payload via REST? should be 10 lines.

ajay: I'll add a test in streaming-harness/tests/stream_recovery_test.py and ping for review.

sara: Thanks all. If we get the change in both runtime and contract this week we can roll a targeted patch next deploy. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks — please post PR links here when ready and tag `eng-platform` for a quick review.

sara: PRs: runtime fix -> https://github.com/redwood/rdw-runtime/pull/182 (draft), contract change -> https://github.com/redwood/api-contracts/pull/432 (WIP).

mike: Nice. I'll skim both and leave notes.

ajay: quick note: if you want to reproduce fast, run the local harness with `--concurrency 50 --batch-window-ms 10`. That was my failure pattern.

oliver: added minimal seq header prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood/streams-proto/compare/seq-header

katie: updated contract PR description to include fallback polling flow and compatibility text.

mike: great progress, moving to async. Ping here when PRs are ready for merge. :raised_hands:
